visible_text: In a circle with centre O, AB is a diameter of length 12 cm. A chord CD of length 6 cm is drawn such that C and D lie on the same side of AB. The shaded region is bounded by the diameter AB, arc AD, chord CD, and arc CB. Find the area of the shaded region. (A) (12π - 9) cm², (B) (12π + 9) cm², (C) (12π - 9√3) cm², (D) (12π + 9√3) cm².
reasoning: The semicircle with radius 6 cm has area ½πr² = 18π cm². The chord CD together with the two radii OC and OD forms an equilateral triangle OCD because all sides equal 6 cm, giving central angle COD = 60°. The area of sector OCD is (60°/360°)πr² = (1/6)·36π = 6π cm². The area of triangle OCD (equilateral with side 6 cm) is (√3/4)·6² = 9√3 cm². The circular segment bounded by chord CD is sector – triangle = 6π - 9√3 cm². The shaded region equals the semicircle minus this segment: 18π - (6π - 9√3) = 12π + 9√3 cm², which matches option D.
